title: Refill and reseal a pantry storage jar
instruction: Remove the green lid from the green storage jar and set it flat on the worktop. Grasp both side tabs of the open cardboard carton and pour the dry grains into the green jar. Keep grains out of the brown jar and off the worktop. Return the carton upright to where it started, then reseat the green lid and release it.
context: Refilling a household dry-food container combines loose-material transfer, spill control and accurate closure. The second jar is an alternate destination.
setup: A wooden 620 × 620 mm worktop with an open 90 × 60 × 126 mm cardboard carton containing 80 dry particles of 7.4 mm diameter, a closed green polymer jar of 104 mm inner diameter and 88 mm height, and an empty uncovered brown polymer jar of 92 mm inner diameter and 82 mm height. The green cap has a shallow locator and a grasp tab. The two fixed-base YAM arms face the worktop. See the README for full dimensions and starting positions.
scoring: Over the final 20 controls, award up to 0.55 proportional to the minimum fraction of grains in the green jar and another 0.20 if all 80 are inside with no mixing or spills. After a qualifying transfer, award 0.15 for the released lid within 4 mm of its seat and 2 degrees of vertical, and 0.10 for the released carton within 18 mm of its starting point and 5 degrees of vertical.
reset_notes: Reset restores all 80 grains to the upright carton and reseats the lid on the empty green jar.
fidelity: The carton, lid and grains are physically simulated as free rigid bodies. The two jars are held fixed to the worktop. The particles approximate dry grains as stiff spheres, and the lid seats using a shallow locating ring. All expert motions use ordinary joint and gripper commands.
